idea: Comparative regulatory research: UK, China and Singapore
buyer: Asset managers and fintechs operating across jurisdictions
pain: Nobody explains three regulatory regimes in one comparable frame
v1: A comparative note on one regulatory topic
verdict: Genuinely useful but she is not a lawyer, and buyers use law firms for this.

why.distribution: Fund contacts are warm but the compliance buyer within them is not her relationship.
why.demand: Inferred; firms use law firms and pay heavily, but that is a different purchase.
why.fmf: She can research and explain, but regulatory comparison without legal qualification has limited standing.
why.defensibility: Accumulated comparative knowledge helps; magic circle firms dominate.
why.ceiling: £1,000/mo x 17 firms = £204k, in a category buyers currently route to law firms.

ceiling_arithmetic: £1,000/mo x 17 subscribers = £204k. Firms buy this from law firms who carry liability; a non-lawyer competes only on framing. Realistic: 4-5 = £48-60k.
carries: A real gap - law firms explain rules, not commercial implications.
kills: No legal qualification, so the output cannot be relied upon in the way buyers need.
test: Ask three compliance heads what they would pay a non-lawyer for comparative regulatory analysis.
test_fail: They say they need something they can rely on legally.
